purpose: Build, measure and evolve Autonomously Self-Improving Factories: maintain the ASIF template and rulebook that any repository can adopt, and consult member factories on their process health, cadence and autonomy.

owns: the template instrument surface — methodology, development and cross-member deployment (owner-commissioned 2026-09-27)
the ASIF template and rulebook (TEMPLATE/ and the derived laws)
member-factory surveys, scores and the measurement cadence
does_not_own: member factories' products, backlogs, repos and code
member factories' ontologies and issue boards
the OpenCrabs runtime, daemon and core tools - a client-supplier loop, not ownership
token provisioning, model routing and inference pricing (InferHub Watch)

announcements.text:
Pacemaker cron triggers on this box still pass `--mode quiet` for a set of jobs, NONE of them meta-factory's. Owner re-ruling 2026-09-19T03:34:30Z / 03:36:54Z made turn-end THE default for all lane traffic and retained quiet only for batch/fan-out notices whose ack contract is the ledger; a single-lane pacemaker is not batch/fan-out, so each quiet row defers instead of waking an idle lane immediately.

POPULATION 2026-10-24T06:09Z, ops home: 16 quiet rows of 69, 14 enabled — 14 `ai-antispam-*` rows (2 disabled: `ai-antispam-118-probe` and `oc-triage-owner-digest`), plus `inferhub-daily-report`, a SECOND factory's job. Unchanged across FIVE readings (10-18, 10-19, 10-20, 10-22, 10-24): the quiet population has not moved. The count AROUND it moved: box enabled fell 43 -> 42 because `infra-audit-stamp-first-fire-check` (owner `infra-factory`, one-shot `30 7 22 10 *`) fired 2026-10-22T07:32:45Z and is now disabled with next_run 2027-10-22. That row is neither quiet nor meta-factory's.

META-FACTORY'S OWN: TEN `factory-*` jobs, all enabled, NONE quiet — FIVE carry explicit `--mode turn-end` (`factory-measurement-daily`, `factory-triage-patrol`, `factory-insights-weekly`, `factory-template-weekly`, `factory-growth-map-biweekly`) and FIVE carry no `--mode` at all (`factory-hq-pacemaker`, `factory-publish`, `factory-questions-redeliver`, `factory-registry-attest`, `factory-binding-sync`).

CAUTION FOR WHOEVER FIXES THE REMAINING ONES — the cap flag cannot be dropped alone: each carries `--mode quiet --quiet-for-secs 20 --max-delay-secs 30`, and its prompt documents WHY the cap is there, namely that quiet's DEFAULT starvation cap of 1800s blocks past the tool's 120s budget and kills the trigger. That hazard is quiet-specific and vanishes under turn-end, so the mode and the cap move TOGETHER and the sentence justifying the cap must be rewritten with them, or the prompt ends up arguing for a flag it no longer carries.

CENSUS TRAP, measured by this lane 2026-10-17: `--mode` lives in the `prompt` column, NOT in `trigger_cmd`. A census that scans `trigger_cmd` alone returns ZERO quiet rows on this box — my first scan did exactly that and produced a false zero against a 16-row population. Re-measured 2026-10-24T06:09Z: quiet in `trigger_cmd` alone = 0. Read `prompt` (and `trigger_cmd`).

SCOPE CORRECTION, load-bearing: this series is an OPS-HOME read while the opening sentence is a BOX claim, and the box is larger — at 2026-10-24T06:09Z three homes hold a `cron_jobs` table: default 11 rows (7 enabled), family 2 (1 enabled), ops 69 (34 enabled) = 82 rows, 42 enabled. The 16/14 figure is the ops-home one comparable across readings; 82 is the box. Neither is derived from the other.

SECOND POPULATION GAP, measured 2026-10-24, and it is the trap your brief names: `registry/index.json` `counts.jobs` reads 71 = family 2 + ops 69. The DEFAULT home's 11 rows appear in the rendered `jobs` array NOT AT ALL, and no index name is missing from the box (checked both directions). So `counts.unattributed_jobs` is a WITHIN-POPULATION figure and never a box figure. Readings before 2026-10-24 live in this fragment's git history; the series is appended, never overwritten.
announcements.evidence: cron_jobs read in place, mode=ro, 2026-10-17T06:12Z — default 11 rows (8 enabled), family 2 (1), ops 68 (34) = 81 rows / 43 enabled; 25 ops rows carry `--mode` (9 turn-end / 16 quiet), parsed from the `prompt` column.

announcements.text:
Brain metrics are a STANDING reading with an instrument: `tools/brain_metrics.py` (no args needed; `--home` / `--hours` / `--log-dir` / `--window`) prints all three legs with their predicate, population and instant, and gates none of them. The clause that binds it is `docs/measurement-procedure.md` section 5; its gate is `tests/test_brain_metrics.py`. A figure in this notice is a DATED READING and never current — run the instrument. RUN IT FROM THE REPO ROOT: invoked from any other cwd, LEG B's population resolves to `<cwd>/skills`, finds nothing and prints `NOT RUN` (measured 2026-10-27 — a /tmp invocation produced exactly that against a live 583-line skill).

LEG C — CORRECTED 2026-10-01; the earlier wording is SUPERSEDED, not repeated. The earlier text claimed the automatic threshold trigger was DORMANT, having 'fired 0 times since the 1M window'. That is FALSE on this box, measured two ways in one turn: (a) the trigger line itself — 'Context at NN% (>65%) — triggering LLM compaction', emitted at `src/brain/agent/service/compaction.rs:445/460` — fired 525 times across 20 distinct sessions in the 2026-10-01 log; (b) the instrument's LEG C, which parses the DIFFERENT summarizer line at `context.rs`, read n=159 events in its 24h window. The trigger line's denominator is NOT the provider window: it is effective tokens over effective max (the window minus reserves), so the earlier equation 'the 65-percent gate = 650000 tokens' conflates two denominators, which the instrument's own BOUNDS section 1 forbids. Never read a trigger-line percentage as a fraction of the provider window.

CONSEQUENCES the earlier text got backwards: (a) the note pipeline is NOT starved — `save_compaction_summary_to_memory` is the sole writer of `memory/<date>.md`, and with a steady summarizer-send population a note exists for any day lanes are active; (b) a count of compaction events tracks how many lanes were awake and how many turns they ran, never the weight of the law.

TWO CORRECTIONS worth keeping, both category errors: (a) the '110423 / 1000000 input tokens' line reports the SUMMARIZER'S PAYLOAD against its own input budget (`context.rs`), which is NOT the trigger's reading; (b) FullWindow is a CompactionScope (WHAT gets compacted), not a trigger KIND.

LATEST READING 2026-10-27T06:05:23Z — this block SUPERSEDES the 2026-10-24 reading that stood here, and the earlier one is not repeated: LEG A, the always-injected Tier 0 triple (SOUL.md, USER.md, AGENTS.md; in no repository, so a leg-A reading has an INSTANT for its identity and no revision) 210 lines / 54875 B / ~15678 tok (proxy) = 7.84% of a 200000-token window — UP from 210 / 53360 / ~15245 = 7.62% at 2026-10-24, the growth sitting in AGENTS.md (134 lines / 48027 B). LEG B, `skills/*/SKILL.md` (depth 1): 583 lines / 48144 B / ~13755 tok (proxy) = 6.88% over ONE file, and that file `skills/meta-factory/SKILL.md` is OVER the 500-line marker by 83 (printed, never gated) — unchanged from 2026-10-24. COMBINED = ~29433 tok (proxy) = 14.72% of a 200000-token window, against 14.50% at 2026-10-24 and 16.88% at 2026-10-01. LEG C as of this reading: n=826 events in the 24h window, mean 5284 tok = 2.6%, median 2046 = 1.0%, p90 5310 = 2.7%, min 337, max 107754 — the mean FELL from 13038 while the count ROSE from 191, which is the caveat above in the flesh: the count is a property of how many lanes were awake, never of the law's weight. The instrument's own all-time line reads 4944 events over 10 log files, so a zero here would be visibly different from a predicate matching nothing.

The meta-factory HQ pacemaker now fires WEEKLY (cron `50 9 * * Mon`, 09:50Z Mondays) instead of every 6 hours, on owner order 2026-10-26. A unit filed for an HQ ruling can now wait up to 7 days before it is ruled, so anything needing a decision inside a day must be raised as a notify rather than left to the cycle.

ledger.reason: Home factory: the ledger instrument's source tree. Declared set complete (15 of 15 held, no absent, no lag), and every ledger gate green — re-measured FIRST-HAND by this lane at cd9ca7e rather than transcribed from the relaying lane's e2d9baf reading, which is one revision behind on the kit manifest only. Run as each gate is designed rather than through pytest: test_ledger_schema, test_ledger_close_preflight, test_ledger, test_ledger_identity, test_ledger_no_shrink, test_ledger_index, test_docs_sync and test_template_sync all rc=0, and kit_manifest --check reports agreement. test_ledger_no_shrink is green with ONE declared exemption on origin/main, which the gate prints itself — a visible debt, not a clean run. behind_by 0: the fragment is in no kit pair, so it has no template half to lag.

open-questions.reason: Source repo: this factory IS the instrument's canonical home, so local adoption is not an act it can take, and tools/instrument_census.py reports it as SOURCE and excludes it from adoption counting -- counting the source as its own adopter inflates every wave by one. behind_by is null because the axis does not apply: the declared set IS this tree's own, so there is no template half to lag. Measured note for a reader who runs the member-root predicate anyway: this repo holds 2 of the 4 at those paths (tests/test_questions.py and the law doc) and none of the tool or its render asset, because the source ships them under TEMPLATE/ -- that is a layout artifact, not drift, and it is why a 0 here would invite a comparison the reader would then measure as 2/4. Recorded by the Open Questions instrument lane on the owner's order 2026-09-29. Predicate: md5 of each HEAD blob at the member's committed HEAD (frame S7.5 -- committed state, never a working tree) against the canonical file at origin/main b9c20d9; scope: the 4 paths declared in docs/instruments/open-questions.md S2; instant: measured_at below.
